MEMORANDUM
  Agenda Item #: 6
  Meeting Date: 4-13-2021

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

THRU:  LAURA GUGLIELMO, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  BRIANNA RINDGE, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  ON MARCH 11, 2021

DATE:  APRIL 13, 2021

ACTION REQUIRED  X  CONSENT  X  RECEIVE & FILE

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council approve the actions of the Parklands Committee
for the meeting of March 11, 2021.

Summary

During the Parklands Committee meeting of March 11, 2021, all Committee Members
were present and one application was discussed.

Analysis and Findings

The City held a Parklands Committee meeting on March 11, 2021 and the Committee
recommended the following action to be approved by the City Council.

1. PC-549-21; Application to remove one Eucalyptus tree located in the parkway
  adjacent to 2548 Via Carrillo

  Applicant: Barbara Pavliscak. 1125 Via Romero. Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Committee Member Groves recused himself due to living in proximity of the project.
Staff introduced the application as a request to restore a partial ocean view, indicating an
existing panoramic view of the ocean and trees. The tree requested for removal is mature,

  1
 safe, and consistent with the neighborhood character, does not provide privacy and does
not significantly block the view.

Mrs. Pavliscak stated she has watched the trees grow for 38 years and advocated that a
balance of neighborhood character and view potential shall be taken into consideration.
Neighbor Casey Crow, supported keeping the mature tree which provides neighborhood
character while a panoramic view already exists.

The Committee discussed safety, designation, and longevity. A majority of the
Committee present supported a balance and agreed a panoramic view already existed.

Chair Richie-Bray reopened public comment to hear Laura Millman’s comments in
support of the application.

Public comment closed and the Committee Members indicated that a balance is
necessary, that the view from the home is beautiful currently, that the tree does not block
the view, and that the diversity of trees on the street is the neighborhood character and
shall be preserved.

Committee Member Cooper motioned and Committee Member McCabe seconded (3-1-1,
Rhodes dissenting, Groves recused) to recommend denial of the application to City
Council.

Notification

These matters have been agenized and posted in the routine manner.

Staff reported prepared by:
Carl Moritz
Urban Forester
